S, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER 1. Accused in Special Case (POCSO) No.2/2024 pending before the Court of Special and II Addl.

District and Sessions Judge, Chitradurga, arising out of Crime No.186/2023 registered by Imangala Police Station, Chitradurga, for the offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376 of IPC, Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and Section 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2016, is before this Court under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023, seeking regular bail.
2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.

NC: 2025:KHC:19856 HC-KAR 3. FIR in Crime No.186/2023 was registered by Imangala Police Station, Chitradurga, initially for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC based on the first information dated 13.11.2023 received from respondent No.2, who is the father of the victim girl aged about 17 years.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced together.
The petitioner, who was arrested on 25.11.2023 was subsequently, remanded to judicial custody.
After completing the investigation, charge sheet has been filed against him for the aforesaid offences.
His bail application filed before the Trial Court in Special Case (POCSO) No.2/2024 was rejected on 22.03.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

4. In the first information which is filed by the father of the victim girl, aged about 17 years, it is stated that the victim girl was found missing from their house on 06.11.2023 and the efforts made to Krishna R vs State Of Karnataka on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112324948/
2 trace her had failed.

sentences.text: Therefore, on 13.11.2023, he had approached the police and based on his first information, FIR was registered against unknown persons.

During the course of investigation,
petitioner and the victim girl were traced together.

Petitioner, who was arrested on NC:
2025:KHC:19856 HC-KAR 25.11.2023 was remanded to judicial custody.

Statement of the victim girl was recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate on 24.11.2023 and in the said statement, she has stated that she was in love with the petitioner and she had gone along with him.
She has not made any other allegations against the petitioner in the said statement.
The victim girl has now been examined before the Trial Court as PW1.
Mother of the victim girl has been examined as PW2 and father of the victim girl has been examined as PW8 in the present case.
PW2 and PW8 have completely turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.

Be that as it may, the fact remains that as on this day, all the material charge sheet witnesses have been already examined and therefore, there cannot be any apprehension that the petitioner may tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
Petitioner, who is now aged about 20 years, is in custody for the last more than 18 months.

Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively without expressing any opinion on merits and demerits of the case.

Accordingly, the following order:-
NC: 2025:KHC:19856 HC-KAR 5.
The petition is allowed.
